LESSON: SIGN READING 7.4.1 INTENSIVE SIGN READING: CHARACTERS IN CLASS READERS.

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade seven
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 7
Topic 7.4: Sign Reading 7.4.1 Intensive Sign Reading: Characters in class readers.
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Sign Reading 7.4.1 Intensive Sign Reading: Characters in class readers., part of Strand 7 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade seven ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: How can you tell the difference between a main and a minor character in a story? 2. How would you describe the behaviour of your classmates?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify minor characters in a class reader,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Sign Reading 7.4.1 Intensive Sign Reading: Characters in class readers. in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. identify signs of vocabulary and phrases used to describe relationships between characters,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Sign Reading 7.4.1 Intensive Sign Reading: Characters in class readers. in the Kenya CBC curriculum.

   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. discuss the relationships between different minor characters in the class reader,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Sign Reading 7.4.1 Intensive Sign Reading: Characters in class readers. in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Sign Reading 7.4.1 Intensive Sign Reading: Characters in class readers. together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Critical thinking and Problem Solving: Learner develops evaluation and decision making skills as they link the relationships between

characters in the class reader to various relationships they are in.

● Communication and Collaboration: Learner develops observing and signing skills as they hot seat different minor characters to bring

out their relationships

Values:
● Social justice: is developed as learners discuss in groups the relationships between characters.

Link to other Subjects

The learner relates the concept of relationship of characters in a class reader to their learning of characterisation in Creative Arts.
